title: DGA and IATSE Push Rob Bonta to Allow Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger With Conditions
description: The Directors Guild of America and IATSE are urging California Attorney General Rob Bonta to settle his antitrust lawsuit with Paramount, arguing th
body:
The Directors Guild of America and IATSE are urging California Attorney General Rob Bonta to settle his antitrust lawsuit with Paramount, arguing that prolonged uncertainty over the Warner Bros. Discovery merger is bad for the industry.

	The two unions wrote a letter to Bonta and Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison on Wednesday, urging the two sides to come to an agreement that would include conditions to address concerns over harms to competition.
	

	“While we have been consistent in our view that mergers, such as this one, historically offer few benefits to workers, we are also particularly concerned about the negative impact a delay in the decision regarding the proposed merger will have on our members and the industry at large,” the two unions wrote.


	The letter puts the two unions at odds with the Writers Guild of America, which filed its own antitrust suit to try to block the merger. The antitrust case has created other divisions within the industry, as both Regal Cinemas and AMC Theatres have endorsed the merger, while the theater trade group — Cinema United — adamantly opposes it.

	Bonta led a coalition of 12 states to sue to block the merger in July, arguing that the deal creates illegal consolidation in the basic cable and theatrical distribution markets. Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin issued a temporary retraining order to pause the deal, and last week set a March 2 trial date, four months later than Paramount’s preferred schedule.

	Ellison has been working to rally support for the deal within the industry,  while also trying to bring pressure on Bonta to come to the negotiating table. Bonta has repeatedly said that he is not interested in “behavioral” remedies — such as a pledge to release 30 movies a year with a 45-day window — but is focused on a structural solution, which Paramount has thus far been unwilling to entertain.
	

	The letter was signed by Russell Hollander, national executive director of the DGA, and by Matthew Loeb, the international president of IATSE. The letter argues that the March 2 trial date is “damaging” to an “already struggling industry.”

	“As our members struggle to find employment, the uncertainty surrounding the proposed merger is only making matters worse,” the letter states. “We are aware of productions that have been put on hold or canceled altogether, leading to further reductions in available work for our members and other industry workers.”

	The letter urges the two sides to agree on conditions, many of which Paramount has already agreed to, such as the maintenance of the two studios as separate entities that will each produce at least 15 films a year. The unions also suggest that Paramount commit to continue licensing content from outside production companies at the same rate as before the merger.

	If the states and Paramount cannot reach a deal, the unions urge them both to agree to an earlier trial date. However, while Paramount has been eager for an accelerated timeline, the states asked the judge for time to depose Paramount executives and obtain documents in order to bolster its case.

schema.headline: DGA and IATSE Push Rob Bonta to Allow Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger With Conditions

title: ‘Reacher’ Season 4 Cast Guide: Who’s Who in the Prime Video Action Series

		‘Reacher’ Season 4 Cast Guide: Who’s Who in the Prime Video Action Series
body:
Aug 12, 2026 4:00pm PT	
	

	
		‘Reacher’ Season 4 Cast Guide: Who’s Who in the Prime Video Action Series
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Courtesy of Prime
	

		
	
				

	Get ready for more action and more Alan Ritchson in “Reacher” Season 4, which premieres Wednesday, Aug. 12 on Prime Video.

	Our hunky, ex-military hero (Ritchson) is once again joined by a slew of new cast members as “Reacher” moves on to a fresh adventure based on Lee Child’s books. Per Amazon Prime, the logline reads: “When a chance encounter with a distraught stranger on a subway goes horribly wrong, Jack Reacher is drawn into a complex and deadly game that pits him against ruthless foes from the highest echelons of power.”

	“Reacher” has a lot to live up to, as Season 3 was Prime Video’s most-watched season on the service since “Fallout” Season 1.

	Whether you’re looking to discover some new faces or just returning to enjoy Ritchson’s screen presence, read below for Variety‘s breakdown of the new and returning faces.


			
			
	Jack Reacher (Alan Ritchson)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Prime				
					
				

	A completely off-the-grid, former Army investigator who leads the series and provides the primary connective tissue between all four seasons. His methods are brutal, and this time around, he dives deeper into a conspiracy than ever before.

	What else you’ve seen him in: “Playdate,” “The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare,” “Ordinary Angels,” “Flipped,” “Fast X”

		
			
			
	Tamara Green (Sydelle Noel)
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	After taking a stand against corruption in her city, this Philadelphia native gets stuck on the night shift and begins investigating a seemingly routine case that doesn’t add up. She’s the kind of investigator who won’t let go of her gut feeling.

	What else you’ve seen her in: “Glow,” “Black Panther,” “Arrow,” “Captive”

		
			
			
	Jacob Merrick (Christopher Rodriguez-Marquette)
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	A small-town cop from New Jersey who travels to Philadelphia in search of answers after his adopted daughter suddenly dies. He isn’t leaving until he has answers.

	What else you’ve seen him in: “Just Friends,” “The Girl Next Door,” “Barry,” “Hawaii Five-0”

		
			
			
	Russell Plum (Kevin Weisman)
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	An off-the-radar investigative journalist who has spent years building a case against the government’s most secretive operations.

	What else you’ve seen him in: “Alias,” “Marvel’s Runaways,” “Scorpion,” “Flipped”

		
			
			
	Lila Hoth (Agnez Mo)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Prime				
					
				

	Lila arrives in Philadelphia in search of her estranged father, a powerful politician. When she and her mother arrive in the city, it sets in motion an unexpected series of events.

	What else you’ve seen her in: R&B singer, Indonesia’s most awarded artist

		
			
			
	Amisha Hoth (Anggun)
			
										
					Image Credit: Shane Mahood/Prime				
					
				

	Once a political dissident who survived atrocities against her country carried out by a power-hungry general, Amisha has sacrificed everything for her daughter, Lila.

	What else you’ve seen her in: “Levitating,” “Cannes Confidential,” “Leo Mattei – Special Unit”

		
			
			
	John Sampson (Marc Blucas)
			
										
					Image Credit: Charley Gallay				
					
				

	Marc Blucas stars as the charismatic congressman, John Sampson, whose secrets are on the brink of being unveiled in Season 4. Currently the frontrunner for his party’s presidential nomination, Sampson was previously stationed in Indonesia for Delta Force.

	What else you’ve seen him in: “First Daughter,” “My Life With the Walter Boys,” “Buffy the Vampire Slayer”

		
			
			
	Elsbeth Sampson (Kathleen Robertson)
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for IMDb				
					
				

	Congressman John Sampson’s wife, Elsbeth Sampson, is played by Kathleen Robertson. As her husband increasingly faces conflict, Elsbeth never leaves his side and is undoubtedly the closest person to John. 

	What else you’ve seen her in: “Boss,” “Scary Movie 2,” “Tracker,” “Northern Rescue”

		
			
			
	Detective Shaun Docherty (Kevin Corrigan)
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Kevin Corrigan stars as Detective Shaun Docherty, Tamara’s cynical partner who’s vocal about his skepticism (but he’s usually right). Although he’s prone to complaining, the dry-humored detective is there for those around him in moments of need, especially Tamara.

	What else you’ve seen him in: “Grounded for Life,” “The Chaperone,” “Hit and Run,” “Pineapple Express”

title: As ‘The Comeback’ and ‘Hacks’ End, Valerie Cherish and Deborah Vance Are Emmy Competitors for the First and Last Time
description: In the Season 5 opener of “Hacks,” Jean Smart’s beleaguered character Deborah Vance is eager to reclaim her legacy — and comes up with the perfect w
body:
In the Season 5 opener of “Hacks,” Jean Smart’s beleaguered character Deborah Vance is eager to reclaim her legacy — and comes up with the perfect way to do it. She wants to be an EGOT.

	The idea of the EGOT — someone who wins all of the “Big Four” entertainment awards at some point in their career (Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony) — has been around for a while but became even more of a talking point as stars and producers began to move between TV, film, stage and music more effortlessly.
	

	In the “Hacks” episode (also titled “EGOT”), Deborah notes that she’s already halfway there. She has a Daytime Emmy for hosting “Begongle,” a game show on the USA Network in 1992 where celebrities played Boggle on a constantly shaking floor. And she has a Tony Award as a producer: “In a post-coital haze, Eric Idle convinced me to put some money into ‘Spamalot’ [which actually won the Tony best musical in 2005].”


	Of course, Deborah is already putting a bit of an asterisk in her EGOT journey, as there’s much debate over whether a Daytime (or News & Documentary or Sports) Emmy counts — or if EGOT should only include the more competitive Primetime Emmy space.

	There are approximately 22 EGOT title holders at present time — but some got there through the Daytime Emmys (like Whoopi Goldberg, Jennifer Hudson and Alan Menken) and others landed there as one of dozens of producers on a Tony-winning play. This year, that was Steven Spielberg, whose Grammy win surprisingly earned him an EGOT — since it was previously undisclosed that he had won a Tony in 2022 as an uncredited producer on “A Strange Loop.”
	

	Add in honorary awards from the Big Four, and the EGOT tally actually climbs to 28. I expect that number to jump even more in the coming years as more stars make EGOT a goal and find random awards categories to try and secure a win. (For non-singers needing a Grammy, the audio book, spoken word or comedy categories might be the best path — as opposed to Deborah’s attempt on “Hacks” to release a Regional Mexican/Tejano album.)

	In “Hacks,” we learn that Deborah was tricked out of a co-creator and writing credit on her 1970s sitcom “Who’s Making Dinner,” or otherwise she might have actually won a Primetime Emmy. Thankfully, Smart has been much luckier — with seven Emmys and counting, plus an eighth very likely on the way. She won two as a “Frasier” guest star in 2000 and 2001 as guest comedy actress, and picked up another in 2008 as supporting comedy actress for “Samantha Who?”

	Then came Smart’s “Hacks” ride, with comedy actress wins in 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025 — every year the show was on the air. If she completes that trick in 2026, Smart will be just one behind Julia Louis-Dreyfus (who has six for “Veep”) for most wins playing the same character on the same show. With five as Deborah Vance, Smart will tie Don Knotts (“The Andy Griffith Show”) and Candice Bergen (“Murphy Brown”) for second place.

	Not a bad run. Smart may not have an EGOT, but she can already boast having EGGS — that’s “Emmy, Golden Globes, SAG-AFTRA Actor.” (Yes, I just made that up.)

	But Deborah Vance isn’t the only fictional Emmy winner on the real-life outstanding comedy actress Emmy ballot. In “The Comeback,” Valerie Cherish (played by Lisa Kudrow) won an outstanding comedy supporting actress Emmy at the end of Season 2, for playing a gritty version of herself in the fictional HBO dramedy “Seeing Red.”

	As for Kudrow, this year reps her third time landing a lead actress nom for “The Comeback” (following 2006 and 2015) and her first in outstanding comedy writing (which she shares with Michael Patrick King). Like Valerie, Kudrow has one Emmy so far — also in the outstanding comedy supporting actress field, for “Friends” in 1998.

	In a Valerie Cherish/Deborah Vance Emmy smackdown, we probably have to give the edge to Deborah, given Smart’s unstoppable winning streak. But no matter how this year goes, with “Hacks” and “The Comeback” ending their storied runs, it’s the last time we’ll get a chance to see those two iconic characters go head-to-head. Hopefully it won’t be the last for the stars who play them.

schema.headline: As ‘The Comeback’ and ‘Hacks’ End, Valerie Cherish and Deborah Vance Are Emmy Competitors for the First and Last Time

title: Phylicia Rashad on Her Historic Career and the Current State of TV: ‘If There’s Something on That I Don’t Like, I Simply Don’t Watch It’
description: Legendary actress, director and producer Phylicia Rashad was the guest speaker at the C-Suite Luncheon during the 24th annual Martha’s Vineyard Afri
body:
Legendary actress, director and producer Phylicia Rashad was the guest speaker at the C-Suite Luncheon during the 24th annual Martha’s Vineyard African American Film Festival (MVAAFF). Started by Stephanie Tavares-Rance, who co-founded MVAAFF along with her husband, Floyd Rance, the luncheon and its accompanying summit uplifts, supports and connects executives, business owners and women leaders of color.

	This year’s luncheon, sponsored by AARP, focused on Rashad’s legacy — from “The Cosby Show” to more recent roles in “The Gilded Age” and the “Creed” movies — and the new study from AARP’s Movies for Grownups, “Bridging the Gap: The Path to More Authentic Portrayals of Black Adults in Movies and TV.” According to the study, Black adults attend movies and consume television and streaming content at higher rates than the general U.S. population. Moreover, the study found that audiences see older Black women as influential cultural figures, and when they are showcased on television, viewers feel more positive about aging.
	

	When asked about her legacy, Rashad mentioned those closest to her. “My mother. My father, my grandparents, the communities in which they were born, and I was privileged to know as a child — that’s what I think about when I hear about legacy, because that’s what flows through,” she told AARP’s CEO, Dr. Myechia Minter-Jordan.


	Looking ahead, Rashad also explained how legacy continues. “It’s something that we become very conscious of. Something that we speak of consciously together. Something we now consciously convey to our young people,” she said. “But it’s really about the way we live. About the way we interact with each other. The way we hold ourselves, think of ourselves — this is what creates legacy. When it came time to play Lena Younger [in “A Raisin in the Sun”], I understood who the woman was. She was not a piece of furniture with a wig on it. She was a woman who knew how to grow things. And I knew that from my greater family. I am so proud of the legacy that has been handed to me. I am so proud of this heritage.”
	

	Though Rashad is perhaps best known for her role as the iconic Clair Huxtable in “The Cosby Show,” she is currently acting in HBO’s “The Gilded Age” and Paramount+’s “Diarra From Detroit.” The Emmy-nominated actress also recently directed the Tony-winning Broadway play, “Purpose.”

	“I love getting a script and going back into history,” she said. “I love learning because I’m looking at humanity and saying, ‘OK. We’ve done this a few times now. Let’s get it right now. Let’s get it right.’ And especially right now, being a human being is so important. I look for the humanity in every world. I’m not considering anything else, and I’m not thinking anything else. This is what my mother taught me. This for me is freedom. I am not circumscribed by anyone else’s idea.”

	When asked how she feels about roles and shows that don’t acurately depict the Black experience she added,  “And if there’s something on television that I don’t like, I simply don’t watch it.“

	Reflecting on her extensive career, Rashad is most proud of the way her work highlights our collective humanity. Whether it’s “Ma Pop, Aunt Esther, Clair Huxtable or whoever,” Rashad said, “I want my work, more than anything else, to demonstrate that as human beings, we are much more alike than we could ever be different.”

schema.headline: Phylicia Rashad on Her Historic Career and the Current State of TV: ‘If There’s Something on That I Don’t Like, I Simply Don’t Watch It’

title: Walt Disney Studios Promotes Melissa Stone to Publicity Chief
description:
Melissa Stone has been named senior VP of publicity for the Walt Disney Studios. 

	She will lead the publicity team and oversee the PR strategy acr
body:
Melissa Stone has been named senior VP of publicity for the Walt Disney Studios. 

	She will lead the publicity team and oversee the PR strategy across theatrical, including Disney Live Action, Disney Animation, Pixar, Marvel Studios, Lucasfilm and 20th Century Studios, as well as Disney+ streaming series. Stone will report to Martha Morrison, the president of marketing at the studio. 


	“I’m thrilled to have Melissa step into this role. She brings more than two decades of exceptional publicity experience, a deep network of talent and media relationships, and a proven ability to lead campaigns that drive both audience engagement and cultural impact,” Morrison said in a statement. “I look forward to seeing her lead publicity across our incredible Studios portfolio.” 
	

	A veteran publicist, Stone has spent 14 years in publicity roles at Fox and Disney. She most recently served as VP of global publicity at Disney after working as a senior publicity at 20th Century Fox. She has led global campaigns including “Avatar: The Way of Water,” “Lilo & Stitch,” “The Little Mermaid,” “The Planet of the Apes” franchise, “The Martian,” “West Side Story” and “Andor.” 


	Disney’s upcoming theatrical slate includes Ridley Scott’s “The Dog Stars” with Jacob Elordi and Margaret Qualley, the animated “Hexed” and Marvel’s “Avengers: Doomsday.” Stone’s focus beyond 2026 will encompass titles like “Ice Age 5,” Ryan Gosling and Shawn Levy’s “Star Wars: Starfighter,” “The Simpsons Movie 2,” “Frozen III” and “Avengers: Secret Wars.”

schema.headline: Walt Disney Studios Promotes Melissa Stone to Publicity Chief

title: Ewan McGregor Says ‘Come On, Disney!’ While Pressuring Studio to Let Him Play Obi-Wan Kenobi Again: ‘They Just Seem Not to Be Ready’
description: Ewan McGregor is putting the pressure on Disney when it comes to playing Obi-Wan Kenobi again. The actor told E! News on the press tour for his late
body:
Ewan McGregor is putting the pressure on Disney when it comes to playing Obi-Wan Kenobi again. The actor told E! News on the press tour for his latest movie, “The End of Oak Street,” that the ball is in Disney’s court regarding his future with the “Star Wars” franchise. McGregor wants nothing more then to continue playing the legendary Jedi. 

	“I’m ready whenever they are,” McGregor said. “They just seem to not be ready, but I’m up for it. At the end of the ‘Obi-Wan’ series, I’m walking off into the desert and I’ve decided to leave. I’ve realized I can’t keep the pressure on Luke. I realized he has to have his own childhood, so I leave him with Uncle Owen and Aunt Beru. And I wander off… and Qui-Gon’s back. And we go off… but where are we going?”
	

	“The next time we find Obi-Wan Kenobi, he’s Alec Guinness up in the mountains,” the actor continued. “What happens between those two moments is what I want to do and spend the rest of my career doing these stories. Stories, you know, series or movies. We’ve got plenty of time; I’ve got 10 years before I am Alec Guinesses’ age. So come on, Disney!”


	McGregor debuted as Obi-Wan Kenobi in 1999’s “Star Wars: The Phantom Menace.” While the movie polarized critics and “Star Wars” fans, most were in agreement about loving McGregor’s performance. He soon became a fan favorite in the galaxy far, far away while reprising Obi-Wan in 2002’s “Attack of the Clones” and 2005’s “Revenge of the Sith.” After a 17-year hiatus, McGregor returned as the Jedi in the 2022 Disney+ streaming series “Obi-Wan Kenobi,” which became the streamer’s second most-watched show of that year with 6.5 billion minutes viewed in the United States (per Luminate). 
	

	While the Disney+ series was always billed a limited series, McGregor has never been coy about his interest in returning for more. “I really hope we do another,” McGregor told British GQ in 2022 before the finale aired. “If I could do one of these every now and again — I’d just be happy about it.”

Hello there, Ewan McGregor! He dives into the stories left to tell of Obi-Wan Kenobi while attending the premiere of his new film, "The End of Oak Street." pic.twitter.com/MuyVM3ALp3— E! News (@enews) August 10, 2026

schema.headline: Ewan McGregor Says ‘Come On, Disney!’ While Pressuring Studio to Let Him Play Obi-Wan Kenobi Again: ‘They Just Seem Not to Be Ready’

title: ‘The Lincoln Lawyer’ Spinoff Starring Cobie Smulders in the Works at Netflix
description:
A spinoff of “The Lincoln Lawyer” starring Cobie Smulders is in early development at Netflix.

	According to Deadline, which first reported news of
body:
A spinoff of “The Lincoln Lawyer” starring Cobie Smulders is in early development at Netflix.

	According to Deadline, which first reported news of the project, the series would center around Smulders reprising her “Lincoln Lawyer” role as Mickey Haller’s (Manuel Garcia Rulfo) half-sister, Artemisia “Emi” Finch. The character debuted in the Season 4 finale of “The Lincoln Lawyer” back in February and is set to return in the upcoming fifth and final season.
	

	Per the description for “The Lincoln Lawyer” Season 5, which will be based on the Michael Connelly novel “Resurrection Walk” and will consist of 10 episodes:


	“Mickey Haller’s (Manuel Garcia Rulfo) world is upended when the half-sister he never knew existed, Emi (Cobie Smulders), comes to him with a plea to help free a wrongfully convicted woman. In a season defined by blood ties and buried secrets, Mickey takes on a grueling habeas petition to overturn a six-year-old murder conviction, but the deeper he digs the more nefarious the forces arrayed against him become. Meanwhile, the stakes rise for his trusted team as Lorna (Becki Newton), Izzy (Jazz Raycole), and Cisco (Angus Sampson) step up to tackle high-profile challenges of their own. Having just saved himself from a wrongful conviction in Season 4, Mickey is now determined to set right an enormous miscarriage of justice. But as he unravels a dangerous web of corruption and lies, he must grapple with the fractured legacy of his family — both his chosen family and the family he never knew he had.”

	David E. Kelley created “The Lincoln Lawyer” for television and serves as executive producer. Ted Humphrey developed the show and serves as executive producer and co-showrunner alongside Dailyn Rodriguez. Connelly, Ross Fineman, Barry Jossen, Tana Jamieson and Matthew J Lieberman also serve as executive producers. A+E Studios produces.
	

	The script for “The Lincoln Lawyer” spinoff is being written by Humphrey, Dailyn Rodriguez and Matthew J. Lieberman, according to Deadline, with A+E Studios producing.

	Netflix declined Variety‘s request for comment on “The Lincoln Lawyer” spinoff news Wednesday.

schema.headline: ‘The Lincoln Lawyer’ Spinoff Starring Cobie Smulders in the Works at Netflix

title: Amazon Game Studios Divests MMOs ‘Lost Ark,’ ‘Throne and Liberty’ in Strategy Shift
description: Amazon Game Studios will return Western territory publishing responsibilities for “Throne and Liberty” and “Lost Ark” to game developers NC and Smil
body:
Amazon Game Studios will return Western territory publishing responsibilities for “Throne and Liberty” and “Lost Ark” to game developers NC and Smilegate, respectively, amid the company’s pivot away from massively multiplayer online games (MMOs).

	“As part of our continued strategic evolution, we have made the decision to transition live operations of ‘Lost Ark’ and ‘Throne and Liberty’ back to their respective development studios. We have tremendous respect for the teams at Smilegate and NC, the worlds they’ve built and the passionate communities that have grown around these games,” Amazon Game Studios said in a statement Wednesday. “We’re proud of what we accomplished together and are committed to ensuring a smooth transition for players.”
	

	Amazon’s games division faced a significant number of layoffs last October amid overall company cuts and strategy shifts across the business, seeing the elimination of 14,000 corporate employees. The choice to divest “Throne and Liberty” and “Lost Ark” comes after Amazon has already indicated its plans to pivot from investing more into the MMO space. The internal focus now is on already planned AAA titles, like the upcoming “Tomb Raider” games, and expanding Amazon’s cloud gaming service Luna through the studio’s “game night”-style party games and its licensed-title business.


	According to Amazon, players of both games will not be directly affected, as data will directly transfer to the video game developers. However, Amazon Game Studios announced in-game mail, friends list memos, blacklist memos, guild member nicknames, stronghold gift messages and chat history will not transfer over for “Lost Ark.”
	

	Accounts will be transferred over automatically, with “Throne and Liberty” beginning later this year and “Lost Ark” beginning early 2027. Active subscriptions will be canceled prior to the transition, but existing balances will carry over. 

	Both Smilegate and NC, which operates under its subsidiary FirstSpark Games, originally created their respective games and will continue their development. 

	There may be downtime during the transition, which Amazon Game Studios will communicate as developments continue. Additional information can be found on the “Throne and Liberty” and “Lost Ark” community pages.

schema.headline: Amazon Game Studios Divests MMOs ‘Lost Ark,’ ‘Throne and Liberty’ in Strategy Shift

title: Charlie Hunnam on His Physical and Vocal Transformation to Play Ed Gein in ‘Monster’
description: It’s a huge responsibility to bring a version of a character to life who was a real person. Throw in the success of a franchise and an infamous seri
body:
It’s a huge responsibility to bring a version of a character to life who was a real person. Throw in the success of a franchise and an infamous serial killer and Charlie Hunnam knew he needed to get his portrayal of Ed Gein right.

	“Monster: The Ed Gein Story,” the eight-part Netflix series, is led by Hunnam as the serial killer who murdered at least two women and exhumed several bodies for his heinous purposes in the 1950s. Raised by an evangelical mother whom he obsessed over, Gein desecrated human cadavers to make a skin suit. His story is rife with disturbing, unprecedented psychological drama and inspired “Psycho,” “The Texas Chainsaw Massacre” and “The Silence of the Lambs.”
	

	Hunnam knew very little about Gein, so when he signed on, he began in-depth research. 


	“It was initially pretty off-putting, because most of the books that have been published about him are these grotesque catalogs, sensationalizing the darker side of who he was and what he did,” says Hunnam, who was fundamentally interested in “understanding what went wrong in the human being that evolved into the monster.”

	That is the essence behind the “Monster” franchise, created by Ryan Murphy. With “The Jeffrey Dahmer Story,” “The Menendez Brothers” and now, with Ed Gein, the series explores true crime through a lens that begs the question: What made the monster, and who is complicit in that evolution?

	To understand Gein, Hunnam gained access to his medical records, which he found most helpful to his portrayal. “He was incarcerated in a mental health facility for almost 30 years and did biannual reviews that were transcribed,” he says. “There were thousands and thousands of pages of his medical history available. So I worked my way through them, and that provided a much clearer, more rounded picture of who he appeared to be, at least to me.”
	

	Corey Castellano, the show’s prosthetic makeup artist, worked with prosthetic artist Mark Nieman to map out what that would look like.  “We started by taking a life cast of Charlie’s face. On the life cast, we sculpted multiple versions of the hooded lid, which we then tested on Charlie,” Castellano says. “Once we found a version that everyone approved of, we began producing them for daily use in a color that closely matched the lightest tone on Charlie’s skin.”



	

	



	It ended up being a small appliance made from thin silicone. 

	“For the actual application, we used a silicone template to ensure that the hooded lid appliance was placed in the same spot each day. The piece was glued on with a medical adhesive, and the edges were blended off with acetone. Once the piece was applied, it was painted using a variety of alcohol-based makeup in thin washes of color to carefully add warmth and match Charlie’s skin tone,” Castellano explains. “For the varying stages of aging, we started by applying the eye and then a forehead, eyebags, crow’s feet, frown lines and nasolabial folds along the side of the nose. The painting process was similar but was finished by adding a bit of silver and gray to his brows to match the wig.”



	

	



	As small as it was, Hunnam says that the psychology of the hooded eye was important in tapping into Gein. “That was something that Ed was very self-conscious about his whole life,” the actor says. “He was bullied about it at school. People would call him flabby face and flabby eye, and Cyclops, and he would cry at school. There were many elements that led to Ed’s isolation and not becoming socially integrated in the way that ‘normal people’ do.”



	

	



	Hunnam adds, “By the time Corey and I met, I was so committed to the idea that this was a huge facet that wasn’t just physical — that it informed his psychology so much in the way he interacted with the world.”

	The actual application process was pivotal.

	“We tried it on, and immediately, I felt like it was transformative. It changed the whole shape, and it was a really important tool,” says Hunnam. “It made Ed feel vulnerable, and with the right attitude, it made him look incredibly sinister.”



	

	



	Although a recording of the night of the killer’s arrest ended up being inadmissible in court, since Gein hadn’t been read his Miranda rights, Hunnam still used it as a tool in order to learn the cadence of his voice. 
	

	“The central thesis for me was a boy who only had one relationship, with his mother, was living in complete isolation outside of that relationship, and if she had told him every day of his life that she hated him because he wasn’t the daughter that she wanted, what would be the manifestation of that?” says Hunnam. “And it seemed plausible to me that he would try to make himself as attractive to her as possible.”

	He also read about abuse and the manifestation of abuse in vocal patterns and took important advice from showrunner Max Winkler. “He said, ‘I keep hearing this mother, mother, sound,’ and he did this high-pitched calling of a mother’s voice, and it was a goose bumps moment,” recalls Hunnam. “I said, ‘That’s so crazy, but you’re pointing me in the right direction with that.’ And that’s how it all came together.”

	It was important for Hunnam that it didn’t “feel like an affectation that was just designed to make this guy feel creepy or a monster.” Instead, he focused on making sure it was “sincere to the idea of what is the manifestation of this guy’s abuse and how is this going to tragically, deeply affect him — which is the precursor to everything else that goes on to terraform his vocal range.”

	Hunnam adds, “He thought if he could become who his mother was, what he perceived his mother always wanted him to be, maybe she would come back from the dead, and he wouldn’t be alone anymore. Which, if you take out the horror of everything that he did, the tragedy of that is too hard to put into words.”

schema.headline: Charlie Hunnam on His Physical and Vocal Transformation to Play Ed Gein in ‘Monster’

title: Bob Chapek, Who Was Ousted as Disney’s CEO, Pens Memoir in Which He Wonders if He Became ‘the Scapegoat’

body:
Bob Chapek is ready to tell his side of the story of his rocky ride as Disney‘s chief executive.

	Chapek has written a 272-page memoir, “Behind the Castle Walls: My Thirty Years at the Happiest Place on Earth.” In it, he “reveals for the first time the high-stakes maneuverings that unraveled behind the scenes from his 2020 appointment to his subsequent dismissal in 2022,” according to an announcement from Simon & Schuster’s Gallery Books, which is publishing the book. It’s set to be released Sept. 29, 2026.
	

	Chapek took over the Disney CEO job in February 2020 — as Bob Iger’s hand-picked successor. But in November 2022, the Disney board ousted Chapek after a series of missteps and called Iger back into service. (Iger stepped down as CEO this March, replaced by former parks head Josh D’Amaro.) 


	Now, after four years of “reflection and distance, Chapek is going behind the scenes of one of the world’s most recognizable — and reticent — companies on earth,” Gallery Books said. The publisher is touting the book as “a revealing and thrilling story of ambition, power and the price of Disney magic.”

	Per the blurb for “Behind the Castle Walls,” within weeks of Chapek’s start as Disney CEO, the COVID-19 pandemic shut down parks, movie theaters and cruise ships — forcing him “to steer the billion-dollar empire through unprecedented times. The stakes were high, the decisions unforgiving, and the backlash often inordinate, leaving him to wonder whether he had become the scapegoat in it all. In 2022, Chapek was out; his former boss was back in.”

	In a 2023 regulatory filing, Disney said its board of directors “determined that Mr. Chapek was no longer the right person to serve in the CEO role” in the months following the renewal of Chapek’s contract in June 2022. “The significant developments and change in the broader macroeconomic environment over this period informed how the board viewed the appropriate leader in light of the rapidly evolving industry and market dynamics. The board therefore concluded that, as Disney embarks on an increasingly complex period of industry transformation, Mr. Iger is best situated to lead the company while an appropriate longer-term successor is identified.”
	

	Chapek’s memoir recounts his formative years growing up in small-town Indiana, where he was raised by his mother and WWII-veteran father. As a kid, “he learned that hard work, dedication, resilience, preparation, curiosity, grit and determination can take you far,” according to the book’s blurb.

	In 1993, Chapek joined the Walt Disney Co. as the marketing director for home entertainment. He went to hold key roles including president of Disney Consumer Products and chairman of Disney Parks, Experiences and Products.

	Variety has reached out to Disney for comment.

            Get ready for a new White House Press Secretary ... President Trump says Karoline Leavitt is stepping down from the job.
      
    
            Trump announced Karoline's upcoming career move in a Truth Social post Wednesday ... saying she's leaving the gig at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her kids and family.
      
    
            Karoline gave birth in May to a daughter ... her second child.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Trump says Karoline will be one of his top outside advisors and continue to be an influential voice within the GOP.
      

            It sounds like this is Karoline's choice ... Trump says he totally understands and respects her decision and praises her as one of the best White House Press Secretaries in American history.
      
    
            Karoline started her current role in January 2025, at the beginning of Trump's second term.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            No word who is on the short list to replace Karoline.
      
    
            Trump had 4 press secretaries in his first term ... and now he will have at least two in his second term.
      
    
            It will be interesting to see who lands the job.
      
    
            Stay tuned ...

            Convicted family killer Chris Watts is hoping to become a married man again ... this time from behind bars.
      
    
            Watts, who is serving multiple life sentences for murdering his pregnant wife and their two young daughters, has reportedly applied to marry Lizzie Henderson, an Ohio realtor he met while incarcerated.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Henderson's relatives told the Daily Mail the couple submitted an application to marry each other while Chris is incarcerated. She has also reportedly begun calling herself "Lizzie Watts" and filed a confidential petition to legally change her name.
      

            Court records seen by PEOPLE confirm a Lizzie Henderson filed a name change case, though the details remain sealed.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Henderson reportedly relocated from Ohio to Wisconsin to be closer to Watts who is housed at Dodge Correctional Institution. She has since become a frequent visitor at the maximum security prison.
      
    
            Henderson confirmed the relationship to the Daily Mail, acknowledging others may find it "weird" but declining to reveal how they met. She said their story is between herself, Watts and God.
      
    
            Watts is serving five life sentences without parole after pleading guilty to murdering his pregnant wife, Shanann, and their daughters, Bella and Celeste, in Colorado in August 2018.

title: Muse Frontman Matt Bellamy Files for Divorce from Elle Evans, Wants Sole Custody
description:

body:
Muse Singer Matt Bellamy
                          Files For Divorce From Elle ...
                          Demands Sole Custody
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                August 12, 2026
                
                            1:41 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 12, 2026
                                2:17 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Muse frontman Matt Bellamy is pulling the plug on his marriage to Elle Evans ... because he just filed for divorce.
      
    
            According to new legal docs, obtained by TMZ, Matt beelined it to Los Angeles Superior Court on Wednesday and filed for divorce after 7 years of marriage.
      
    
            The exes share 2 children ... a 6-year-old daughter and a 2-year-old son ... and Matt is asking the court for sole legal and physical custody of the kids.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Elle tells TMZ ... she will fight for custody of their kids, and Matt made the marriage so "unbearable" the divorce filing was "a long time coming."
      

            He says they have a premarital agreement and wants the judge to award spousal support to Elle pursuant to the terms of their prenup.
      
    
            Matt and Elle tied the knot in August 2019 in Malibu.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The exes announced their separation in mid-2025. He said the breakup was due to "really unexpected circumstances."
      
    
            In his divorce filing, Matt cites "irreconcilable differences" as the reason for the split ... and he says the date of separation is "TBD."
      
    
            Matt was previously engaged to Kate Hudson until 2014 ... and the exes share a kid.
